sections.h2: Coking coal imports fell 39% in dollar value from the FY2022-23 peak

chart.title: Dollar value of coking coal imports fell every year after the FY2022-23 peak
chart.sub: US$ million, HS 27011910 'Coking coal'. FY2025-26 is provisional.

sections.means: The decline tracks falling global coal prices rather than India needing less coking coal, since Ministry of Coal volume targets still rise.
sections.todo: DGCI&S should report coking coal imports by country of origin as well as consignment, so trade-hub figures can be checked.

sections.h2: Australia's US$5,110.92 million outweighs the USA, Singapore and Russia combined

chart.title: Australia supplied far more coking coal value than any other source in FY2025-26
chart.sub: US$ million, FY2025-26 provisional, HS 27011910. Singapore and Switzerland are trading hubs, not mine origins.
chart.source: DGCI&S TradeStat, Commodity x Country report.

sections.means: Australia's supply is concentrated, while Singapore and Switzerland likely overstate their role as mine-of-origin suppliers.
sections.todo: DGCI&S should publish country-of-origin data so readers can see where Singapore's US$1,430.14 million coking coal actually comes from.

sections.h2: Six thermal plants face ₹61.85 crore compensation for missing biomass co-firing targets

chart.title: Talwandi Sabo accounts for more than half of the ₹61.85 crore
chart.sub: Compensation imposed by CAQM on 8 April 2026, for FY2024-25 co-firing shortfalls. Unit: ₹ crore.

sections.means: Six plants in Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh were penalised for missing FY2024-25 co-firing targets under the Delhi-NCR track.
sections.todo: The Ministry of Power and CAQM should issue one joint notice stating the co-firing percentage that applied in FY2024-25, since the sources give 3% and 5%.
